report.summary: All three UI tests failed with a 5s timeout on `page.goto('/books')`. The app's `list_books` has a random 0–8s sleep, so the page is only sometimes slow. Remove the sleep first, then rerun to check the tests pass.

causes.title: Random 0–8s sleep in list_books makes /books exceed the 5s navigation timeout
causes.explanation: `list_books` calls `time.sleep(random.uniform(0, 8))`, and `render_books` calls it on every GET /books. Roughly 37% of loads (anything over 5s) therefore exceed Playwright's 5000ms goto timeout. The outcome depends on chance, so the same code could pass on a rerun. The app is only sometimes slow, so this is flaky rather than a product bug. I did not read the CI logs or the other tests, so I can't say whether this is injected on purpose or left over from debugging. The three UI tests that open /books hit it together. Tests that don't render the book list, such as login and most API tests, are unaffected.
evidence: app/main.py:256: "books": list_books(user["id"]) (used when rendering the /books page)
playwright._impl._errors.TimeoutError: Page.goto: Timeout 5000ms exceeded. navigating to "http://127.0.0.1:49185/books", waiting until "load"
causes.suggested_fix: Remove the random sleep from `list_books`. If latency is deliberately simulated, make it deterministic and short, or turn it off in the test environment (for example with an env flag). Don't paper over it by raising the test timeout.
